messages:
maya: FYI noticed a bunch of traces with root span but no child spans for requests routed through the new router canary. Happening since the 11:22 deploy.
jon: ugh, saw that too. exporter logs show 503s around the same time. could be backpressure but the pattern looks like propagation loss.
sasha: any chance the router stripped trace headers? we switched proxy implementation in canary and it defaults to drop some headers.
maya: that's my suspicion. sampled root spans exist, but downstream services report new trace IDs. traceparent missing.
rory: telemetry-bot alerted about span counts dropping ~60% for the router->backend path. alert details: `span_count drop >50%`
telemetry-bot: automated note: from 1768452200 to 1768453800, span ingest decreased by 57% for service=api-router, sample_rate unchanged. exporter error rate spiked 12%.
jon: attaching a quick tail of the router access log showing incoming headers and proxied request:
```
# incoming request
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
content-type: application/json

# proxied outbound
# (note: traceparent header missing)
content-type: application/json
```

sasha: that matches. new proxy lib requires explicit header_preserve = ["traceparent","tracestate"] or it drops them.
maya: i can repro locally by flipping header_preserve off. Jon, can you check the canary config?
jon: confirming: canary deployed with proxy v2.0.3 and default config (we accidentally omitted header_preserve in the k8s config map).
rory: deploy-bot shows the canary rollout timeline:
```
deploy-bot: rollout started 1768452000
deploy-bot: canary scaled 10% at 1768452100
deploy-bot: canary scaled 50% at 1768452300
deploy-bot: canary scaled 100% at 1768453200
```

maya: so header drop window exactly aligns with scale-up. We should pin canary back/patch config. Recommend patch: set header_preserve to include traceparent and tracestate and roll canary back to 0% while patching.
jon: +1. i'll patch the config and trigger a restart of proxy pods. is there a quick workaround in the routing rules to append trace headers from the request context?
sasha: risky to synthesize IDs. better to preserve upstream headers. generating new trace IDs will break correlation and sampling decisions.
maya: agree. also ask infra to check exporter retries — 503s may be secondary due to volume changes, but main cause is missing children.
rory: i'll open an incident ticket and run a retention check on the trace store for the affected window. if any child spans were ingested but mis-attributed, we can try re-linking by parent_id heuristics, but likely not worth the complexity.
telemetry-bot: incident created: T-3452 - missing-child-spans-after-router-deploy. paging oncall.
jon: patch applied to config map, setting header_preserve = ["traceparent","tracestate"], rolling restart started.
maya: watching spans — dashboards refresh in a min.
jon: restart finished, router pods back up with new config.
telemetry-bot: span ingest trending back to baseline for service=api-router (now +3% vs baseline).
maya: verified downstream services now show same trace IDs and children present. closing loop: will add a unit test for header preservation in canary harness and update rollout playbook to include trace header smoke check.
sasha: i'll add the test to CI and a console dashboard alert for sudden parent/child ratio drops.
rory: note for postmortem: consider exporter backpressure metrics (queue length, 503s) as a correlated signal but primary root cause = header preservation config.
maya: thanks team. :thumbsup:
